text: With the Excel check clean, it's time to publish — and now that there's a real finding, decide whether this stays the one-time analysis lesson one scoped, or becomes a living report.

Publishing to the Power BI Service uploads the report and the dataset behind it, but because the source is an on-premises SQL Server, the Service can't reach it directly without an on-premises data gateway standing in between.

Daily refresh would be overkill — a customer's churn status barely moves day to day. The real decision is monthly, timed a few days after month-end close, so a full month of orders is actually there to refresh against.

Access gets scoped just as carefully: the Sales Director gets Viewer access through a Power BI App, not full workspace membership — she can see the report and use the Southeast bookmark, but she can't edit the model.

Moving from a one-time analysis to a recurring monthly report is a real scope change from what was agreed in lesson one, so it gets a short confirmation email, not a silent decision made on her behalf.
The dashboard is live, refreshing monthly, with access scoped correctly. Next up: a different kind of problem — a number that didn't match finance's own report.
